title: Review: Real vs ideal gases and kinetic molecular theory; Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Kp; Maxwell–Boltzmann and catalysts; Concentration and standard solutions
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM03#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM03#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM03#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM04#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM03#N.9, AM04#N.12, AM06#N.5, EQ04#N.7c, KN03#N.3b, AM03#N.7, AM04#N.10b, AM06#N.7, EQ04#N.3b, KN03#N.12, AM03#N.3b, AM04#N.15a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Concentration
items.clue: Amount of solute divided by the volume of the whole solution.

items.label: Volumetric flask
items.clue: Glassware filled until the bottom of the meniscus sits on the mark.

items.label: Dilution
items.clue: Adding water, which changes the volume but not the amount of solute.

items.label: Pressure
items.clue: Caused by gas particles hitting the walls; it doubles when the volume is halved.

questions.stem: A student adds 600.0 mL of water to 200.0 mL of 0.500 M NaCl(aq), giving 800.0 mL of solution. What is the molarity of NaCl in the diluted solution?
A rigid 2.50 L container holds a mixture of 0.200 mol of He(g) and 0.300 mol of Ne(g) at 127 °C. What is the partial pressure of Ne in the container?

options.text: 1.25 atm
3.28 atm
3.94 atm
5.80 atm

questions.stem: A rigid container holds a mixture of He(g) and Ar(g) at 300 K. A student claims that the He atoms and the Ar atoms have the same average speed, because the two gases are at the same temperature. Which evaluation of the student's claim is best?

options.text: It is correct: the temperature of a sample measures the average speed of its particles, whatever the mass.
It is correct: the particles in a sample at one temperature all move at one speed, whatever their mass.
It is incorrect: the average speed of a particle is set by its mass, and does not depend on temperature.
It is incorrect: the two average kinetic energies are equal, and the He atoms have the higher average speed.

questions.stem: 3 Fe(s) + 4 H₂O(g) ⇌ Fe₃O₄(s) + 4 H₂(g). Which is the expression for Kp?

options.text: Kp = (P_Fe₃O₄)(P_H₂)⁴ / ((P_Fe)³(P_H₂O)⁴)
Kp = (P_H₂)⁴ / (P_H₂O)⁴
Kp = (P_H₂O)⁴ / (P_H₂)⁴
Kp = 4P_H₂ / 4P_H₂O

questions.explanation: Only the gases appear: H₂ on top, H₂O below, each to the power 4.

questions.stem: A reaction energy profile for an elementary reaction plots energy against the reaction coordinate. What does the reaction coordinate represent?

options.text: The time that has passed since the reactants were first mixed together
The fraction of the reactant molecules in the sample that have become products
The progress of the atoms' rearrangement from the reactants into the products
The distance that the reactant particles travel before they collide

questions.explanation: It is the axis along which the set of motions that rearranges reactants into products is plotted.

questions.stem: A student prepares 100.0 mL of 0.200 M CuSO₄(aq) by placing 3.19 g of CuSO₄(s) in a 100.0 mL volumetric flask, dissolving it in some distilled water, adding distilled water to the mark and mixing. The molarity of the solution is later found to be less than 0.200 M. Which of the following could explain this result?

options.text: The flask still held some distilled water from rinsing when the CuSO₄ was added.
Water was added until the bottom of the meniscus was above the mark.
Half of the solution was poured into a beaker before its concentration was measured.
The CuSO₄ dissolved completely, so no solid could be seen in the flask.

questions.explanation: Overfilling makes the volume more than 100.0 while the amount stays 0.0200 mol, so c = n/V falls.

questions.stem: A weather balloon holds 5.00 L of helium at 1.00 atm and 25 °C. It rises to where the pressure is 0.500 atm and the temperature is −23 °C. Assuming no gas escapes, what is its new volume?
questions.explanation: V₂ = 5.00 × (1.00/0.500) × (250.15/298.15) = 8.39 L. Expansion from the pressure drop wins over shrinkage from cooling.

questions.stem: A sample of N₂(g) in a rigid container is heated from 300 K to 600 K. Which statement correctly describes the change?

options.text: The peak of the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gets taller, so the entropy of the gas decreases.
The Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gets lower and broader, so the entropy of the gas increases.
The curve keeps its shape and shifts right, as every molecule's energy doubles.
The curve gets broader, so more molecules have exactly the average energy.

questions.explanation: Energies spread over a wider range, so energy is more dispersed: entropy rises. The area under the curve stays the same.

questions.stem: A rigid flask contains N₂(g). Some Ar(g) is then added to the flask while the temperature is held constant. Which statement about the partial pressure of N₂ after the Ar is added is correct?

options.text: It decreases, because the mole fraction of N₂ falls while the total pressure stays the same.
It stays the same, because the amount of N₂, the volume and the temperature are unchanged.
It increases, because the Ar atoms collide with the N₂ molecules and drive them into the walls.
It becomes equal to the partial pressure of Ar, because the two gases share the total equally.

questions.stem: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen can stay unchanged at room temperature for years. In Döbereiner's lamp (1823), a jet of hydrogen in air strikes a piece of platinum and reacts at once, with no flame or spark to start it. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The platinum heats the gas, so the curve moves to higher energy and more molecules exceed the same Ea.
The platinum gives a route with a lower Ea, so at the same temperature far more molecules have enough energy.
The platinum makes the reaction more exothermic, so the molecules gain the energy they need to react.
The platinum changes the shape of the curve, moving its peak to higher energy without heating.

questions.stem: A student dissolves 17.1 g of sucrose, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ (molar mass 342.3 g/mol), in 40.0 mL of water. The volume of the resulting solution is 50.5 mL. What is the molarity of sucrose in the solution?
A sealed aerosol can is left in a car on a sunny day. At 20 °C the gas inside is at 3.00 atm. The can warms to 70 °C; its volume stays constant. What happens to the pressure inside the can?

options.text: It rises to 3.5 times its starting value.
It stays the same, because the volume is fixed.
It rises by about 17%.
It falls by about 15%.
